text: Davidson's central thesis in 'Actions, Reasons, and Causes' (1963) is that:
choices: The reason for which an agent acts is also a cause of the action
Reasons explain actions but never cause them
Actions are uncaused, wholly free events
Only bodily movements, not reasons, can explain behaviour
explanation: Davidson argued that the reason for which one acts is a cause of the action: what distinguishes the reason that explains from a reason one merely has is that the former actually caused the behaviour. Option 1 is the anti-causalist view (Anscombe/Ryle) he opposed, option 2 is libertarian, and option 3 is behaviourist.
